H1.note: chain starts at C4-locus variation; the C1QA claim is the mechanism's ('C1QA supplies the classical-pathway initiation machinery'); CX3CR1 is listed but is in no H1 step and the mechanism gives it no direction ('regulates')

H2.note: the chain ends at 'abnormal complement-dependent synapse elimination', never schizophrenia, so the second claim targets that end node. The step H2.3 is unsigned, but the claim's sign comes from the mechanism ('permits excessive C1Q/C4-dependent synapse handling'; the falsification expects CSMD1 loss to increase synapse loss). 'Complement-dependent' is the mechanism named in passing, so the node is synapse pruning (GO:0098883, as in H1; GO:0150062 complement-mediated synapse pruning is its child)

H3.note: 'low C1QA or impaired CX3CR1 ... causes' the disease: both neg

H4.note: 'NXPH3 disruption' is loss: neg. The chain ends at cognitive and sensorimotor dysfunction, never schizophrenia; second claim targets the expressible end node

findings.detail: H3 claims low C1QA raises schizophrenia risk, while H1.2 and H1.3 of the same run say C1QA drives synapse elimination which raises risk; H3's C1QA claim composes only through H1's statements, with the opposite sign
H2.2 ends at the classical complement pathway, H2.3 starts again at CSMD1 ('loss of CSMD1 complement restraint'); the complement-to-synapse-elimination link H2 needs is never stated

H3 is three disjoint fragments: C1QA to abnormal synaptic maturation, CX3CR1 to microglial physiology and synapse maturation, mistimed microglial circuit maturation to schizophrenia; no step's object is the next step's subject
H4.1 ends at alpha-neurexins, H4.2 starts at loss of NXPH3 signaling; H4.2 ends at abnormal spatial learning and startle, H4.3 starts at 'NXPH3-dependent synaptic circuit dysfunction'
H4 ends at 'schizophrenia-relevant cognitive and sensorimotor dysfunction' and never reaches schizophrenia; its title does not name the disease
H2 ends at 'abnormal complement-dependent synapse elimination' and never reaches schizophrenia
these steps lead to 'abnormal' nodes although the mechanisms state a direction (excessive synapse handling for H2, delayed pruning for H3), so the chains carry no sign where the text does

H3.3's subject 'mistimed microglial circuit maturation' is a vague disjunction ('delayed or spatially inappropriate' pruning) with no term, so the only H3 step that reaches schizophrenia cannot be stated

the three GWAS rows report SNP-disease association, not C4 expression; the SNPs sit in C2 (rs116385615), EHMT2 (rs142520578) and TNXB (rs1150754), not in C4A or C4B, and none of the rows gives the step's direction

the sources summary says rs142520578 has 'mapped gene C4A' and rs1150754 'mapped gene C4A, C4B', but the records' author-reported genes omit C4A (rs142520578, intronic in EHMT2, C4A 88 kb away) or are TNXB alone (rs1150754)
rs116385615 and rs142520578 are associations with the cross-disorder trait 'Autism spectrum disorder or schizophrenia', not schizophrenia
PMID:22632727 shows microglial engulfment depends on CR3/C3 in the retinogeniculate system; it names neither C1q, C4 nor CSMD1

PMID:26814963 implicates excessive complement activity in schizophrenia and notes fewer synapses in patients ('may help explain'); it never states that synapse elimination causes the disease, so H1.3 has no support
the CSMD1 GWAS rows give association only; the run's own note admits the SNP-to-loss-of-function direction is untested; rs6986895's risk allele is unreported ('?')

PMID:38301948, H3's central source, reports lower C1QA in schizophrenia (an association) but is cited for C1QA loss causing abnormal synaptic maturation; no H3 step carries the C1QA-schizophrenia association it actually reports
PMID:38301948, cited as contradicting H1, says in its background that C4A contributes to synapse removal, which supports H1.2 for C4A; it is attached as support there

PMID:42000733 (listed as contradicting) says C4A, in contrast to C4B, is implicated in pruning, refuting the C4B half of H1.2; H1 still lumps C4A/C4B (its note admits paralogue specificity is unresolved)
HPA:ENSG00000168329 (CX3CR1, microglia) and HPA:ENSG00000173372 (C1QA, microglia) are supporting citations for H1 and H3 that no step uses
Q96PZ7 (CSMD1 UniProt: 'Potential suppressor of squamous cell carcinomas') and HPA:ENSG00000183117 support no step; the CSMD1 UniProt text does not mention complement
HPA:ENSG00000183117 is listed as both supporting and contradicting evidence for H2
the mechanism says NXPH3 is 'expressed in human excitatory neurons', but HPA gives 6.6 nCPM there against 29.8 in smooth muscle cells, and tissue enrichment in blood vessel above brain
rated high, but only the C4A half of H1.1 has a cited text that states it, H1.2 for C4A rests on a mouse result cited for another step, H1.3 has no support, and C1QA's role has none

rated medium, but no cited text states any step on a route to either H3 claim: S9 has no support, H3.1 and H3.3 are unexpressed, the C1QA route borrows H1's unsupported S3 and S6 with the opposite sign, and S10 (the only supported H3 statement) is on no route; its central paper PMID:38301948 reports only lower C1q in patients, finds C1QA co-expression networks not enriched for risk variants beyond C4A, and says the functional implications are unknown
almost every run entity has an empty CURIE; schizophrenia is given as 'EFO:MONDO_0005090', an EFO prefix on a MONDO id; yet every hypothesis says support 'grounded'
CCDC136 is in the question's gene list and in no hypothesis; the run reports it as unexplained
BLN:C4-schizophrenia-associated-variation stands for the run's class of C4-locus risk alleles (structural and SNP), which has no single dbSNP or ClinVar id
BLN:CSMD1-schizophrenia-associated-variation stands for the run's class of CSMD1 risk alleles; the two cited SNPs are instances, one with an unreported allele
HP and MP have no 'abnormal synapse maturation' or 'abnormal synapse pruning' term (only zebrafish ZP:0009310), so two steps fall to no_sign under the undirected-change rule

a null result against a hypothesis claim (GWAS:NXPH3:no-association, no NXPH3 variant associated with schizophrenia) has no statement to refute when no step reaches the disease, so it can only be excluded and never weighs against H4
'X is required for normal Y' has no direct form; written as X lowering the MP 'abnormal Y' phenotype

the exclusion table lists an MGI 'abnormal X' annotation as no_direction, but when the statement's target is the 'abnormal X' phenotype itself (undirected-change rule) the knockout annotation does state the step; kept as curatedDb
claims about human NXPH3 and CX3CR1 target MP (mouse) phenotypes because HP has no spatial-learning, startle-reflex or microglial-physiology abnormality term
one mouse C4 result supports both human C4A and C4B statements; the taxon flag cannot say the mouse gene is the ortholog of both paralogues, so the same quote counts twice

one MGI knockout annotation (curatedDb, taxon mouse) makes S14 and S15 'established' (belief 0.8) for human NXPH3, and S10 too with a 'By similarity' line, while S1, a human expression-by-allele result in Nature, gets 0.5; the mouse-to-human gap does not discount the annotation

PMID:38301948's background sentence has C4A acting 'through signaling within the C1q initiated classical activation axis', which could bridge classical complement to synapse removal for H2, but its subject is C4A and H2 never signs that link; not added

audit.before: category no_sign: 'subject is an undirected change ... so the step has no sign'
audit.after: category ungroundable: the step is signed (+); its subject 'mistimed microglial circuit maturation' has no term and is a vague disjunction
audit.reason: no_sign means a causal step with no direction anywhere, but H3.3 is 'leads_to, positive'; an 'abnormal' or 'mistimed' subject still carries a signed effect (the curator wrote S16 with an 'abnormal synaptic transmission' subject). What fails is the node, not the sign

audit.before: one claim (csmd1RiskVariation →+ schizophrenia risk); note: end node 'has no sign and no term, so no phenotype claim can be written'
audit.after: second claim added: csmd1RiskVariation →+ process synapsePruning (GO:0098883); note rewritten
audit.reason: the guide asks for an end-node claim when the chain never reaches the disease. A claim's sign comes from the title and mechanism, not the step: the mechanism says the alleles 'permit excessive C1Q/C4-dependent synapse handling'. A term exists: synapse pruning, with 'complement-dependent' as the mechanism named in passing (GO:0150062 complement-mediated synapse pruning is its child). The claim has no route, like claim 1

audit.item: findings undirected_step and missing_term (H2.3, H3.1, H3.3)
audit.before: both findings counted H3.3 as an undirected step falling to no_sign
audit.after: H3.3 removed from both; new ungrounded_label finding for H3.3's vague subject
audit.reason: follows the H3.3 recategorisation: H3.3 leads from a 'mistimed' node, not to an 'abnormal' one, and its step is signed

H3 is rated medium, but no cited text states any step on a route to either claim. Its C1QA route borrows H1's unsupported S3 and S6 with the opposite sign. Its central paper, PMID:38301948, reports only lower C1q in patients and finds no risk-variant enrichment for C1QA networks beyond C4A
